# Terraform AWS Network Firewall Route Association Module

 [![Latest Release](https://img.shields.io/github/release/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-nfw-route-association.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-nfw-route-association/releases/latest) [![Last Updated](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-nfw-route-association.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-nfw-route-association/commits)


AWS Terraform module that associates route table entries with AWS Network Firewall VPC endpoints for the supplied endpoint subnets and firewall sync states.

## Introduction

This module resolves the route table attached to each supplied endpoint subnet and creates an `aws_route` entry that points traffic to the AWS Network Firewall-managed VPC endpoint in the matching Availability Zone.

Use it when you already have an AWS Network Firewall deployed and need deterministic route propagation from endpoint subnets to the correct firewall endpoint IDs.

## Usage


**IMPORTANT:** The `master` branch is used in `source` just as an example. In your code, do not pin to `master` because there may be breaking changes between releases.
Instead pin to the release tag (e.g. `?ref=vX.Y.Z`) of one of our [latest releases](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-nfw-route-association/releases).


Bootstrap a deployment directory with Terragrunt scaffold:

```sh
# 1. Create and enter the target deployment directory
mkdir -p <environment>/<region>/<spoke>/nfw-route-association
cd <environment>/<region>/<spoke>/nfw-route-association

# 2. Scaffold the module
terragrunt scaffold github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-nfw-route-association

# 3. Edit the generated inputs file
vi inputs.yaml

# 4. Review and apply
terragrunt plan
terragrunt apply
```

Example `inputs.yaml` for the generated deployment folder:

```yaml
endpoint_subnet_ids:
  - "subnet-0123456789abcdef0" # (Required) Subnet ID for the endpoint AZ.
  - "subnet-0fedcba9876543210" # (Required) Subnet ID for another endpoint AZ.

endpoint_destination_cidr: "0.0.0.0/0" # (Optional) Destination CIDR routed through the firewall endpoint. Default: 0.0.0.0/0.

nfw_states_list:
  - availability_zone: "us-east-1a" # (Required) Must match the AZ of one endpoint subnet.
    attachment:
      - endpoint_id: "vpce-0123456789abcdef0" # (Required) Firewall endpoint ID for us-east-1a.
  - availability_zone: "us-east-1b" # (Required) Must match the AZ of one endpoint subnet.
    attachment:
      - endpoint_id: "vpce-0fedcba9876543210" # (Required) Firewall endpoint ID for us-east-1b.
```

Example `terragrunt.hcl` wiring generated values into the module:

```hcl
terraform {
  source = "github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-nfw-route-association?ref=v1.0.1"
}

locals {
  local_vars = yamldecode(file("${get_terragrunt_dir()}/inputs.yaml"))
}

inputs = {
  endpoint_subnet_ids       = local.local_vars.endpoint_subnet_ids
  endpoint_destination_cidr = local.local_vars.endpoint_destination_cidr
  nfw_states_list           = local.local_vars.nfw_states_list
}
```

## Quick Start

1. Collect the endpoint subnet IDs for the route tables you want to update.
2. Extract the firewall sync states, including each `availability_zone` and `attachment[].endpoint_id`, from the AWS Network Firewall deployment.
3. Fill in `inputs.yaml` and run `terragrunt apply`.


## Examples

Typical use cases:

- Centralized egress VPCs where private subnet traffic must traverse AWS Network Firewall endpoints.
- Shared-services network topologies where firewall endpoint IDs are obtained from another Terragrunt stack or remote state.
- Multi-AZ deployments where each endpoint subnet must map to the firewall endpoint in the same Availability Zone.

## Inputs

| Name | Description | Type | Default | Required |
|------|-------------|------|---------|:--------:|
| <a name="input_endpoint_destination_cidr"></a> [endpoint\_destination\_cidr](#input\_endpoint\_destination\_cidr) | Destination CIDR block to route through the AWS Network Firewall endpoints. | `string` | `"0.0.0.0/0"` | no |
| <a name="input_endpoint_subnet_ids"></a> [endpoint\_subnet\_ids](#input\_endpoint\_subnet\_ids) | List of subnet IDs whose associated route tables should receive a route that targets the AWS Network Firewall VPC endpoint in the same Availability Zone. | `list(string)` | `[]` | no |
| <a name="input_extra_tags"></a> [extra\_tags](#input\_extra\_tags) | n/a | `map(string)` | `{}` | no |
| <a name="input_is_hub"></a> [is\_hub](#input\_is\_hub) | Establish this is a HUB or spoke configuration | `bool` | `false` | no |
| <a name="input_nfw_states_list"></a> [nfw\_states\_list](#input\_nfw\_states\_list) | AWS Network Firewall sync states keyed by availability zone, typically sourced from firewall\_status[0].sync\_states. | `any` | `[]` | no |
| <a name="input_org"></a> [org](#input\_org) | n/a | <pre>object({<br/>    organization_name = string<br/>    organization_unit = string<br/>    environment_type  = string<br/>    environment_name  = string<br/>  })</pre> | n/a | yes |
| <a name="input_spoke_def"></a> [spoke\_def](#input\_spoke\_def) | n/a | `string` | `"001"` | no |
